body:
ACCEPT — no named seam belongs to a different stage. I rechecked the current source, and no relevant source path changed between the audit's 07d1aa94 base and current e887c692.

Evidence:

- NarrativeCompilerInput.of still takes StorySource + SurfaceAtlas, sentence-keyed PropositionEvidence, and SpanSet-backed Evidence; it rejects atlas/source/receipt checksum disagreement and validates evidence spans against the canonical text.
- StoryModel still stores StorySource and SurfaceAtlas directly; supporting and covering return/consume text SpanSet.
- AlignmentSource.sourceSupport is Option[SpanSet], while align.NodeSummary.support is a mandatory SpanSet.
- FeatureTarget has only Token, Sentence, Situation, Segment, Boundary, Turn, Window, and SurfaceUnit. SupportResolver and FeatureObservation remain text-SpanSet based.
- AudioSpan is nonnegative integral milliseconds and permits [t,t). TranscriptAtlas checks text order and only compares adjacent present audio start times; it permits audio overlap and turnAtAudio returns the first match. That is exactly a legacy text/interview overlay, not a complete cinematic time model.
- A repository-wide Scala-source search still finds no SourceBundle, PresentationAxis, EvidenceSupport, NarrativeSourceAtlas, or MediaAtlas.

One interpretation must stay explicit when C1 is eventually scoped: C1 may define NarrativeSourceAtlas and the text/timed-transcript conformance adapters, but it cannot claim that the existing compiler consumes the new atlas yet. NarrativeCompilerInput/StoryModel/alignment/features migration remains D1, as the audit says. The C1 gate proves the new portable substrate and exact preservation/refusal laws in isolation; D1 proves integration.

On that reading, ACCEPT the measured boundary and stage ownership. P1 and aggregate B0 remain entry blockers. No C1 implementation, source read, dependency, API migration, or file edit is authorized by this review.
